alt: The sixteen MYP key concepts in three groups. Four are contributed by individuals and societies: change, global interactions, systems, and time, place and space. Culture, development and communities are named as often important in the subject. Nine others complete the set.
caption: Four key concepts belong to I&S, three more often help, and nine complete the MYP set.

alt: Three linked boxes. Cause: defeat in the Crimean War exposed Russia’s backwardness. Process: reform from above by decree, the 1861 Emancipation Manifesto. Consequences: about 23 million serfs freed in law, but too little land and 49 years of redemption payments fed unrest, an unintended result.
caption: Describe change through all three: causes, process and consequences.

alt: A schematic of the Blue Nile flowing from Ethiopia, where the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam was built from 2011 and inaugurated in September 2025, downstream to Sudan and Egypt, which raised concerns about how much water would reach them.
caption: Interdependence: an upstream decision changes what downstream states receive.

alt: A drainage basin as an open system. Precipitation is the input; soil water, groundwater and lakes are stores; infiltration, throughflow and surface runoff are flows; river discharge and evaporation are outputs. Deforestation cuts interception, so runoff is faster and flood peaks higher.
caption: Name the parts of a system and show how a change to one affects the rest.

alt: Left: Singapore’s absolute location as a point on a grid at a latitude of about 1 degree north. Right: its relative location, off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula beside the Strait of Malacca, a busy shipping lane between the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
caption: Where a place is in relation to others often matters more than its coordinates.

after: ## From concepts to a statement of inquiry
alt: Three ingredients, key concept systems, related concepts scarcity and sustainability, and global context globalization and sustainability, combine into one statement: when people take more from a natural system than it can replace, the system and dependent communities can be damaged. Checks: no named place or date, uses all the concepts, links to a global issue.
caption: One key concept, related concepts and a global context make one transferable sentence.

alt: Three tests in sequence. If a textbook settles it, the question is factual, such as which countries border Lake Chad. If it works for a different place unchanged, it is conceptual. If informed people could argue opposite answers with evidence, it is debatable, such as whether a government should put farm exports ahead of a local fishing industry.
caption: Three quick tests sort any inquiry question.
